idiom_name: tokio::net::TcpListener accept loop + TcpStream::connect; hyper/tower service
implementation_notes: std has no async I/O; the pattern is realised through a runtime: TcpListener::bind + accept().await is the acceptor, TcpStream::connect() the connector, per-connection tasks the handlers. Frameworks (hyper/axum) collapse the accept loop behind a service abstraction, leaving only handler code.
pitfalls: Blocking work in an async task starves the runtime; use spawn_blocking for sync code.
Spawn-per-connection is unbounded; gate accepts with a semaphore (Semaphore::new(n)).
Treat file-descriptor exhaustion (EMFILE/ENFILE) as recoverable back-pressure, not as a panic — log and back off.
Graceful shutdown needs a cancellation token (tokio::sync::broadcast/oneshot) plus draining of in-flight tasks; use JoinSet to track and await all spawned tasks.
The borrow checker prevents sharing a TcpStream across async tasks; use Arc<TcpStream> or restructure to move ownership explicitly.
accept() returns (Conn, std::net::SocketAddr); ignoring the remote address loses useful diagnostic information.
